install.from source: git clone https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git && cd openclaw && pnpm install && pnpm ui:build && pnpm build
install.note: Prefer the official installer, which handles Node provisioning and package-manager compatibility. Current install docs require Node 24.16+ (24.x) or 26.1+ and recommend Node 26. For a manual npm install, check `node --version`, `npm --version`, and `npm view openclaw@latest engines --json`: the published package can differ from the docs. npm 12 blocks lifecycle scripts by default; npm 11.16+ accepts --allow-scripts=openclaw, while older npm must omit it. Do not run interactive onboarding inside shell_exec.

install_flow.summary: Install without onboarding, verify the CLI, then hand first-run onboarding to the user’s terminal.
agent_steps: Detect OS and architecture. Use the matching official installer with --no-onboard / -NoOnboard in a non-interactive shell.

For manual npm installation, check the Node engine range of the package being installed and the npm version before choosing the command. With an approved registry mirror, append --registry=https://registry.npmmirror.com to that same version-appropriate command.
Run `openclaw --version` after installation. A successful package install does not confirm Gateway setup.

For a fresh install, tell the user to run `openclaw onboard --install-daemon` in their own terminal. Do not start this interactive wizard through shell_exec. Preserve an existing installation’s configuration; an upgrade does not automatically require onboarding again.

verify: openclaw --version   # confirms the binary is on PATH; `openclaw onboard` must still be run once (see install_flow)

mirrors.npm: After the user confirms the mirror fallback, append --registry=https://registry.npmmirror.com to the npm command selected for their npm version; retain --allow-scripts=openclaw on npm 11.16+ / 12.
